key_insight: Medical image encoders become more similar mainly when they are trained with self-supervised objectives, not simply because they are larger or clinically supervised.
clinical_relevance: A classifier can transfer across encoders and hospitals, but the shared representation is only partial and should be validated before assuming models are interchangeable in practice.
method: Compared 18 image and 7 text encoders across 5 imaging modalities, spanning 7M to 27B parameters.
Controlled training to vary only the learning objective while keeping data, architecture, and scale fixed.
Tested representational similarity plus transfer across encoders, modalities, and five held-out hospitals.
evidence_signal: On chest radiography, matched self-supervised encoders aligned most (40.4%), while label-supervised (21.1%) and image-text (3.3%) were much lower; transfer retained about 85% of within-encoder performance.
watch_item: The convergence is modest, within-modality, and does not match clinical similarity judgments, so interoperability may fail in weaker subgroups or settings.
paper_title: Self-supervision drives representational convergence in medical foundation models more than clinical supervision
